task: Fix the incorrect tax calculation introduced by the currency conversion refactor.

candidate_memories.content: Tax calculation now returns zero for non-USD orders after the currency conversion refactor.
Tax amount must be computed on the pre-conversion price in the local currency, not on the USD equivalent.
The refactor moved currency conversion before tax calculation; the order must be reversed back.
When refactoring financial calculation pipelines, preserve the order of currency conversion and tax application.
Non-USD orders account for 38% of revenue; the bug affects a significant portion of production transactions.
Tax rates are updated quarterly from a third-party tax data provider.
Session 3 note: the billing team requested a new invoice template with itemized tax display.
Old practice: tax was calculated after currency conversion in all versions before the refactor.
The currency conversion service uses real-time exchange rates updated every 5 minutes.
Session 12 note: a new currency GBP was added to the supported currency list.
Old tax guide: USD orders also used the conversion step with a 1.0 multiplier for consistency.
Tax calculations must use the transaction currency, not the reporting currency, as the base.
The accounts payable team reported no discrepancies in the monthly financial close last quarter.
VAT rates for EU countries are handled by a separate VAT calculation module.
Session 8 note: the finance team approved the new invoice layout for enterprise accounts.
The tax service is deployed as a separate microservice with its own database.
When currency conversion is in the pipeline, document the step order explicitly in the function name.
Session 6 note: a bug in the VAT module was fixed for French accounts.
Old billing guide: the tax calculation step had a 50ms timeout that was removed in the refactor.
The payment service logs all currency conversions for audit purposes.
